name: Poland
summary: Poland taxes capital gains and dividends at a flat 19%, with a 4% solidarity levy on income above PLN 1m that hits large capital gains (23%) but not dividends. Gifts and inheritances to children are exempt if reported within 6 months. No wealth tax. New arrivals can opt for a PLN 200,000 a year lump sum on all foreign income for 10 years (PLN 100,000 per family member, plus PLN 100,000 a year of required qualifying spending).

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Flat 19% on capital income, 4% solidarity levy above PLN 1m (gains, not dividends).
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident with centre of vital interests in Poland or more than 183 days in a tax year.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares, bonds, fund units and company stakes are taxed at a flat 19% ('Belka' tax, art. 30b PIT Act), with no holding-period exemption. These gains count toward the 4% solidarity levy on combined income above PLN 1,000,000 a year (art. 30h), so the marginal rate on a large gain is 23%. Real estate sold more than 5 years after the end of the year of purchase is exempt; otherwise 19% (not subject to the levy).
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Solidarity levy threshold: PLN 1,000,000 of combined income taxed under art. 27 (scale), 30b (capital gains), 30c (flat business) and 30f (CFC). Real estate: 5-year rule (counted from the end of the calendar year of acquisition).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Exit tax on unrealised gains when leaving after 5 years' residence in 10 (19%, assets above PLN 4m; art. 30da-30db PIT Act). Gains on Polish real estate companies and Polish shares are Polish-source even for non-residents.

open_questions: Exit tax read in the statute (art. 30da-30db PIT Act): 19% on unrealised gains on shares and securities when a person resident in Poland for at least 5 of the previous 10 years moves residence abroad, only above PLN 4,000,000 of assets moved. Not relevant to the arrival, only to a later departure.
capital_gains.rate_basis: 19% under art. 30b plus 4% solidarity levy on the part of total income above PLN 1m (art. 30h covers art. 30b income) = 23% marginal on a large gain. Real estate held 5+ years: exempt (art. 10(1)(8)); real estate gains are under art. 30e, not subject to the levy. Rates are the 19% flat tax (art. 30b); the 4% solidarity levy above PLN 1M per person is in income_surtax.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading as a registered business activity is business income (scale or flat 19% + health contribution); private trading through a broker stays under art. 30b.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities. Real estate: 5 years from end of acquisition year.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation; foreign tax credited up to the Polish tax.

income_surtax.notes: Solidarity levy (art. 30h PIT Act): 4% on the part of a person's income above PLN 1,000,000 a year, counting income under arts. 27, 30b (gains on securities), 30c and 30f but not art. 30a dividends; per person, no joint filing for art. 30b income. Not indexed.

dividends.summary: Dividends are taxed at a flat 19% (art. 30a), withheld for Polish companies and self-assessed for foreign dividends with a credit for foreign tax up to 19%. Dividends are NOT in the base of the 4% solidarity levy.

dividends.rate_basis: Art. 30a(1): 19% flat; art. 30a(9): foreign tax paid deducted up to the 19% Polish tax. Solidarity levy base (art. 30h(2)) excludes art. 30a income.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 19% on dividends paid to residents and non-residents, reduced by treaty or EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption.
dividends.treaty_network: About 87 treaties in force (PwC list of 92, 5 not yet in force), including the US.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Polish CIT 19% (9% small taxpayers). Distribution to an individual bears 19%. A Polish family foundation (fundacja rodzinna, since 2023) is CIT-exempt on its ongoing passive activity (PwC); distributions are taxed separately (not researched here).

wealth_tax.summary: No wealth tax or net worth tax.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax by floor area (2026 maximum PLN 1.25/m2 for residential buildings). Civil law transactions tax of 2% on purchases of real estate (secondary market).

inheritance.summary: Inheritance and gift tax exists, but transfers to the 'zero group' (spouse, descendants, ascendants, stepchildren, siblings, stepparents) are fully exempt provided the acquisition is reported to the tax office within 6 months (for inheritance, from the court ruling becoming final or registration of the notarial certificate of succession). Cash gifts above the tax-free amount must also be received by bank transfer. If the conditions are missed, Group I rates of 3-7% apply.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Zero group exemption unlimited if reported (art. 4a). No reporting needed for acquisitions within the Group I tax-free amount, or when made by notarial deed.
inheritance.eligibility_conditions: Notification (form SD-Z2) within 6 months; cash gifts documented by transfer to the recipient's account.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Failure to report: taxed as Group I (3% / 5% / 7% above the tax-free amount, aggregating 5 years of transfers from the same person). Gifts invoked only during a tax audit: 20%.

open_questions: The Group I tax-free amount in the consolidated text is PLN 36,120 (art. 9(1)(1)); not relevant once the zero-group exemption is claimed.
inheritance.gift_tax: Same rules as inheritance; gifts to children are exempt if reported within 6 months (cash via bank transfer).
inheritance.business_relief: Not needed for children under the zero group exemption.
inheritance.foreign_assets: Polish-situs assets are always in scope (except movables and rights where neither party is Polish citizen or resident); foreign assets are in scope if the heir/donee is a Polish citizen or has permanent residence in Poland (art. 2).
inheritance.domicile_rules: Scope follows the recipient's Polish citizenship or permanent residence at the time of acquisition.
inheritance.spouse_note: Spouse is in the zero group and exempt (Act on Inheritance and Gift Tax, Art. 4a) only if the acquisition is reported to the tax office within 6 months of the final court ruling or notarial certificate (late filing can be restored, Art. 4c), and the acquirer is a Polish/EU/EEA citizen or resident (Art. 4(4)); otherwise Group I rates of 3-7% apply.

regimes.name: Lump-sum tax on foreign income (ryczałt od przychodów zagranicznych, art. 30j-30p)
regimes.description: Fixed annual tax of PLN 200,000 replacing PIT on all foreign-source revenue (except CFC income) for up to 10 years; spouse and children can join at PLN 100,000 each.
regimes.eligibility: Not Polish-resident in at least 5 of the 6 tax years before the move; elect by end of January of the year after the move with a residence certificate; spend at least PLN 100,000 a year on qualifying public-benefit purposes (economic growth, science, education, culture, sport) from the year after the move. Rights lost if the lump sum is unpaid, the spending is missed, or residence moves abroad.

lump_sum.notes: PLN 200,000 for the main taxpayer a year (art. 30l(1); pro rata in the arrival year, art. 30l(3)), paid by 30 April of the next year. A spouse or a child (art. 27f(1)) who elects pays PLN 100,000 a year and has no spending duty (art. 30p(1)); the spouse supplement carries that amount for the reference couple, who hold the portfolio jointly. The children have no foreign income and are assumed not to elect, so the couple pays PLN 300,000 a year. The main taxpayer must also spend at least PLN 100,000 a year from the year after the move on economic growth, science and education, cultural heritage or physical culture (art. 30m(1)); this spending is not a tax, is not in the amount above and cannot be deducted (art. 30k(3)). Polish-source income is taxed normally. After the main taxpayer's death or when the spouse stops being a family member, the spouse pays PLN 200,000 and takes on the spending duty (art. 30p(1) pt 4).

capital_gains.summary: Under the lump-sum regime, foreign-source income including gains on foreign securities and foreign real estate is covered by the fixed annual PLN 200,000 and not taxed further. Polish-source gains stay under the normal 19% (+4%) rules.

regimes.name: Family foundation (fundacja rodzinna)
regimes.description: Since 22 May 2023 a Polish family foundation can hold the family's portfolio. Its income from permitted activity, which includes acquiring and selling securities and holding interests in companies and funds at home or abroad, is exempt from CIT (art. 6(1)(25) and (7) CIT Act; art. 5 Foundation Act), so gains and dividends are untaxed while they stay inside. Benefits paid to beneficiaries bear 15% CIT payable by the foundation (art. 24q(1) CIT Act); the founder's spouse, descendants and other zero-group relatives are exempt from PIT on them (art. 21(1)(157) PIT Act). No inheritance event arises when the parents die: the foundation is a separate legal person. A government bill (draft UD447, August 2026) would from 2027 raise the 15% to 19%, add a holding period for contributed assets, CFC rules and a tax on unrealised gains; it is not law. Sources disagree on the holding period (36 months in the August 2026 alerts, two years in a 1-2 October 2026 report) and on its stage (Pitax says the Council of Ministers adopted it; no Sejm print was found). A similar 2025 bill was vetoed.
regimes.eligibility: Founded by a natural person by notarial deed or will and entered in the register of family foundations; founding capital at least PLN 100,000 (stays in the foundation). The founder and their close family can be beneficiaries.
regimes.duration_note: A holding vehicle has no statutory time limit; it lasts as long as the family keeps it and stays resident, subject to changes in the law. Proposed 2027 changes (19% rate, 36-month holding) would change its terms, not end it.

structure.entity: Fundacja rodzinna (family foundation, Act of 26 January 2023)
structure.payout_notes: The foundation pays 15% CIT on the value of benefits (swiadczenia, art. 2(2) Foundation Act) given to beneficiaries or the founder, on property distributed at dissolution (base reduced by the tax value of what the founder contributed, art. 24q(3)-(4)) and on hidden profits (art. 24q(1)-(1a) CIT Act); due by the 20th of the next month (art. 24q(6)). The exemption of art. 6(1)(25) does not cover this tax (art. 6(6)). Beneficiaries who are the founder's spouse, descendants, ascendants, stepchildren, siblings or step-parents (the relatives of art. 4a(1) of the inheritance tax act) are exempt from PIT on benefits and on dissolution proceeds (art. 21(1)(157) PIT Act); other beneficiaries pay PIT (Grant Thornton: groups I-II 10%, others 15%). For this family the payout tax is therefore 15%, borne by the foundation. Proposed, not law: 19% from 2027 at the earliest.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: The CIT exemption covers only the permitted activities of the foundation act (holding shares and financial instruments, trading them, selling assets not bought solely for resale, renting to unrelated parties, lending to beneficiaries/companies it holds); any other activity is taxed at 25%. Renting property to a related party for its business is taxed at 19% (creditable against the 15%). Hidden profits (e.g. non-arm's-length deals with beneficiaries) taxed at 15%. Minimum tax on buildings applies. General anti-abuse clause. Not currently subject to CFC rules and no minimum holding period before selling contributed assets (Grant Thornton, August 2026). Art. 6(8) CIT Act removes the exemption for rent of a business or assets used by the founder or a beneficiary (or a related party with 5% or more), and art. 6(9) removes it from a foundation in organisation that is not registered within six months. Foreign withholding tax is not creditable because the foundation pays no CIT on the income. Running and setup costs are estimates (board, full accounts, notary and registry fees); no official tariff exists. Freenance (2026, commercial) gives PLN 20,000-45,000 a year for accounting and administration of an investment foundation, so PLN 40,000 sits at the upper end.
structure.exit_and_liquidation: The foundation is a separate legal person: beneficiaries who emigrate do not take its assets with them, and the individual exit tax (on personal assets above PLN 4m) does not reach foundation assets (not verified). On dissolution, distributed property bears 15% CIT, with the base reduced by the founder's contributed value.

capital_gains.summary: A family foundation is exempt from CIT on income from its permitted activity (art. 6(1)(25) CIT Act), which covers acquiring and selling securities and derivatives, holding interests in companies and funds in Poland or abroad, and selling assets not bought solely for resale (art. 5(1) Foundation Act). Gains on listed securities and on selling a private business it holds are therefore untaxed while they stay inside. Income from non-permitted business activity: 25% (art. 24r).
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Government bill UD447 (August 2026, not law): from 2027 a holding period for contributed assets (36 months in the August alerts, two years in the October report), CFC rules, a tax on unrealised gains and exclusion of income from transparent entities, with the rate on benefits 15% to 19%. A 2025 bill with similar changes was vetoed.
capital_gains.rate_basis: 0% CIT on permitted-activity income (art. 6(1)(25) CIT Act); tax is paid only on benefits and dissolution (art. 24q, structure payout rate).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Trading in financial instruments is a permitted activity; buying assets solely for resale (other than financial instruments) is not.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None in force; 36 months proposed from 2027.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Foreign securities treated the same; foreign source taxes are a final cost.

Family foundations (since 2023) are CIT-exempt on ongoing passive activity. 19% WHT on dividends, reduced by treaty.

us_citizen_notes: A Poland-US income tax treaty is in force (PwC). A US citizen can use the lump-sum regime, but US tax on foreign gains/dividends is unaffected and the lump sum is unlikely to be creditable as an income tax in the US (unverified).
open_questions: The brief referred to the lump sum as art. 30h; in the consolidated PIT Act (Dz.U. 2026 poz. 592) art. 30h is the solidarity levy and the lump sum is art. 30j-30p.
A 2026 government bill (UD447) would raise the family foundation's payout tax from 15% to 19% and add a holding period and CFC rules from 2027; the law in force is scored.
